title: Vinod Kumar v. State of U.P.
coram: Manoj Kumar Gupta, J.; Vikram D. Chauhan, J.
disposition: Writ disposed on undertaking to withdraw theft recovery and issue a fresh provisional assessment.
headnote: In a writ against a theft-of-electricity recovery notice, the Allahabad High Court treated an assessment issued on a printed provisional-assessment proforma but headed as a final assessment as a patent abuse of power showing no application of mind. After the Executive Officer undertook to withdraw the recovery and assessment and to issue a fresh provisional assessment, concluding proceedings strictly under the Electricity Supply Code, 2005, the Court disposed of the petition in those terms.
facts: Vinod Kumar challenged a recovery notice dated 14 September 2022 issued in an alleged theft-of-electricity case by Electricity Urban Distribution Division-XI, Varanasi. The assessment under challenge was on a printed proforma meant for a provisional assessment order, though headed as a final assessment. After an adjournment and a connected listing with Writ-C No. 37137 of 2022, the Executive Officer filed an affidavit that the recovery and the assessment would be withdrawn and a fresh provisional assessment issued. The Division Bench then disposed of the petition.

reusable_constructions.construction: An assessment issued on a printed proforma meant for a provisional assessment, but headed as a final assessment order, is a patent abuse of power and discloses no application of mind.

holding_units.topic: theft assessment — provisional proforma issued as final order
holding_units.holding: A theft assessment issued on a printed proforma meant for a provisional assessment order, but headed as a final assessment, is a patent abuse of power and shows no application of mind. Where the licensee then undertakes to withdraw the recovery and the assessment and to issue a fresh provisional assessment, concluding the proceedings strictly in consonance with the Electricity Supply Code, 2005, the writ challenging the recovery notice is disposed in terms of that stand.

principle_tags.application: Applied to a 14.9.2022 theft recovery notice issued on a printed provisional-assessment proforma headed as a final assessment; the Court called that a patent abuse of power, and disposed of the writ on the licensee's undertaking to withdraw the recovery and assessment and to issue a fresh provisional assessment under the Electricity Supply Code, 2005.

not_decided.point: Merits of the theft allegation and quantum of assessment
not_decided.note: The Court did not decide whether electricity had been stolen or what charges were due; proceedings were to restart with a fresh provisional assessment under the Supply Code, 2005.
